gapsClosed: A current account canceled in its cooling-off was asked only whether anything used it (linkedTo), so one overdrawn closed with its debt, and one with money on its way, card payments pending or savings beside it closed too. It's asked Close It's own refusals (closeRefusal) now.

Your Accounts Over Time offered Cancel It for savings and cards only, so the command's current-account branch had no control. A new current account other than the primary is offered, its Close It refusal said under it with the button grayed out.

A current account canceled in its cooling-off closed with no interest paid and no fees charged, and its overdraft limit left on it, where Close It (closeNow) settles both and the guide said it “closes the same way”. It is settled as Close It settles one now: settleInterest, settleFees, the limit cleared; in Canada the charges for its operation while it was open come back (SOR/2021-181 s.5(2)), where Britain (BCOBS 6.3.2R) and Germany (BGB § 357b(2)) let the bank charge for the service provided. Fees past what it holds with its interest are refused (cancelRefusal), which the panel reads too. Its words on the panel say what comes back.

Canceling kept a savings account’s or term deposit’s interest from it everywhere, and paid a current account’s everywhere. It follows the country’s rule now: kept in Britain and Canada; returned, any already paid posted back with its tax and off the year’s income, in the EU/EEA countries and Mexico.
Canada’s refund of charges covered only a current account; it covers any deposit account now, and Mexico’s with it.
Korea’s deposits had a 14-day cooling-off its rule (금융소비자보호법 제46조) doesn’t give; removed, cards kept.
Close It closed a German account overdrawn by its closing fees; refused now, as Cancel It refuses it.

A term’s interest taken during the term (bank.take_term_interest) went into the primary account, and Cancel It took it back out of there, but cancelRefusal counted only interest paid into the term itself, so nothing refused it and a Commerzbank primary was left at −€6.30 (Postbank −€6.08). interestBackOf now counts each payment by the holder’s account it went into, and cancelRefusal refuses while any of those holds less than goes back out of it. Deutsche Bank’s own terms say only that each side repays what it received within 30 days (its ZinsMarkt Widerrufsfolgen), nothing of keeping it back from the deposit, so it’s refused rather than taken from the term.

Canada’s refund took every bank fee since opening, overdraft interest among them (it’s posted as a bank fee against Overdraft Interest), where SOR/2021-181 s.5(2)(b) refunds charges “other than interest charges”; and it was all credited against Bank Fees. chargesBackOf now leaves out a charge against Overdraft Interest and returns each charge by the expense line it was charged to, which the refund credits.

Canada’s 14 and Mexico’s 10 days were counted as calendar days; their rules count business days (SOR/2021-181 s.5(1); LTOSF art. 11 Bis 1, “diez días hábiles”). coolingOffEnds counts them with afterBusinessDays in the bank’s country and the holder’s region; inCoolingOff and the panel’s “until” date read it (the panel had used the panel bank’s country’s days).

A Canadian card had a 14-day cooling-off. Bank Act s.627.11 lets a credit card agreement be canceled “in accordance with any prescribed requirements”, and SOR/2021-181 prescribes them for a retail deposit account (s.5), a deposit-type instrument (s.6) and the products s.4 lists, no card among them (read 2026-10-15). inCoolingOff is false for a Canadian card.

Mexico’s right holds only “siempre y cuando el Cliente no haya utilizado u operado los productos o servicios financieros contratados” (art. 11 Bis 1, read 2026-10-15 at diputados.gob.mx, last reform 14 November 2025); SLATE didn’t ask. SLATE can tell: usedSince counts a payment out of the account by its holder, a card’s purchase among them, and not the bank’s fees, its interest or its tax; money paid in isn’t counted, an account being funded to be opened (SLATE’s reading). A used Mexican account is out of its cooling-off.

A term’s interest taken during the term was found on canceling by its memo alone, “Interest: FestzinsSparen”, which every term at the bank shares, so canceling a new term took back what an older one had paid: out of the primary, off the year’s income, and counted in the refusal (€6.93 in the skeptic’s probe). bank.take_term_interest now carries the term itself in a posting of nothing, interestPaidSince finds a term’s payments by that posting, and the reversal leaves the zero posting out. Interest taken before the fix carries no such posting and isn’t found on canceling (in a save from before it, that interest gets no refusal and no reversal).

The cooling-off period ended at the hour the account opened on its last day (openedAt + days, or afterBusinessDays at the same hour), though Directive 2002/65/EC art. 6(1) gives 14 calendar days, SOR/2021-181 s.5(1) “within 14 business days after the day on which [it] is opened”, and LTOSF art. 11 Bis 1 “diez días hábiles posteriores”, and the panel named the day: an RBC account “until January 23” was refused at 11:30 AM on the 23rd. coolingOffEnds returns the last moment of that day in the save’s zone (endOfDay), and the panel names the date in that zone.

The New Haven half (no Cancel It, the refusal, the account kept) is proved; abroad the card branch (London), the current-account branch and its refusals are proved, the panel drawn while a refusal holds (the reason under it, Cancel It grayed with the same words), and three defects are fixed: a current account is settled on canceling as Close It settles one (its interest paid, its fees charged, in Canada its fees refunded), each part played abroad. From the later pass of 2026-10-15: canceling follows each country’s rule on interest (kept in Britain and Canada, returned in the EU/EEA countries and Mexico) and on charges (refunded for any deposit account in Canada and Mexico); Korea’s deposits have no cooling-off; and Close It refuses a German account its closing fees would overdraw, as Cancel It does. Mexico’s half of both rules and the German interest tax’s reversal are tested. From that day’s second recheck, two more defects fixed abroad: a term’s taken interest is found by the term itself, not by the name every term at the bank shares, so canceling a new Deutsche Bank term no longer takes back an older one’s (Berlin); and the period runs to the end of its last day, as each rule counts it, not to the hour the account opened (Toronto, Berlin). The refusal’s one-cent threshold is tested. Each FIXTURE, as no played life banks outside the US.

gapsClosed: A Fail’s notice told every student ‘at the year’s end you can ask to repeat the year’, even in a year already repeated, where repeatRefusal refuses a second time. It now offers that only where the year can still be repeated. (Until the second round that meant a year not in repeatedYears; since then, a year with room in the nine semesters as the year’s end counts them, which takes in a year repeated.)

A Fail at an evaluation that dismissed the student (the faculty’s review, or the warning unmet) or withheld the degree was still told to ask to repeat the year at its end, which “You’re not at school.” then refused: the notice was said in settleCourses, before the evaluation read the Fails. It is said by tellFails after the evaluation settles the standing, with the School’s ending read, and so after the standing’s own notice at the same instant.

A Permanent Incomplete in a year repeated once already was told to ask to repeat the year. It isn’t now: until the second round by a `repeated` check, since then by the count of semesters (`repeatOpen`, as `tellFails`).

After any repeat granted, a Fail or a Permanent Incomplete in any later year, at an evaluation that ended nothing, was still told to ask to repeat the year at its end, which “Repeating would make 10 semesters…” refused: the notices excluded only the year itself being repeated. They now read repeatRoom, the count as the year’s end will make it: those enrolled, the program’s terms still to be taken through that spring (the spring at a fall’s evaluation, the year’s two again after a repeat is granted), the year’s two again and the terms after (withRepeat). The caller’s first version counted those enrolled so far, which at a second fall’s evaluation after a first year’s repeat made nine and still offered; the terms to come were added on 2026-10-15. The `repeatedYears` clause in repeatOpen was then redundant (enrolled is the program terms taken plus two per repeat granted, so the count is 8 plus 2 per repeat) and was removed.

A year split by a leave lost its fall’s Fail: repeatCourses picked the year’s courses by calendar term (the spring and the calendar term before it). A two-term leave begun at a spring, the only length leaveLengths grants from one, puts the year’s fall three calendar terms before its spring, so a fall Fail or Permanent Incomplete was dropped and the year’s end refused “Every course this year was passed: there’s nothing to repeat it for.”, after the notice (and the faculty’s review, “the year is to be repeated”) had offered it. It now picks by program term (`academic`, the record’s term less the offset before it). The request’s calendar terms (Repeat.terms) are the spring and the last term enrolled before it, not the calendar term before (yearTerms); nothing reads them yet. The other calendar-adjacency readers were checked: none in courserecord.ts or school.ts reads a course’s year by calendar; yearKeyOf (school.ts) groups work-study hours by the calendar’s academic year, the aid year they’re counted in, and was left.
